beats.headline: Something extra from loot-all
beats.text: The Skull Empire hunter called The Talent has zapped himself with his own Lightning scroll. Carl tells Donut to loot him, so he will not pay that much in tithe taxes, and she gasps: almost 75,000 gold and three scrolls of Lightning. When she hits loot all she gets something extra that was not listed: a credit chit. It looks like a credit card and has no description. They need to go buy something with it before they cancel it, she says. Hold onto it for now, Carl tells her; they will ask Mordecai. And from now on, loot hunters one item at a time.

beats.headline: Credit chit and all
beats.text: An unaffiliated hunter, a level-50 dreadnought merchant, opens his mouth to scream, and Carl kicks him in the nuts. He lands on the man's chest and breaks his neck by the twin horn stubs, out of sight of the guards. Into the inventory goes the body. It doesn't have much, but it does have one of those weird credit chits, like the one taken off the orc several days earlier. From what Carl gathers, they are the equivalent of intergalactic credit cards.

beats.headline: From the dead pig
beats.text: Rosetta has her hand on the eye tattoo on Carl's chest and is demanding his toraline out loud. In chat, where they cannot hear, she asks something else: does he still have the credit chit he got from the dead pig? It is the card they looted off the orc hunter on the sixth floor, and Donut has it in her inventory. Good, Rosetta writes. She will get it from her.

beats.headline: Robbing a king
beats.text: Carl brings King Rust's dripping head to Rosetta in the smoke, and she presses it to a pad on a device like a hand-held credit card machine. Something beeps. She tosses the head back to him and tells him to take the corpse too. Then she pulls a long, plastic-like card from the device, tosses it to the ground, slams in a similar one and presses a button. A happy little beep. Is that the credit chit? Donut asks. Are you robbing him? You said we needed a password!

beats.headline: Not on the chit anymore
beats.text: In the liaisons' room, Orren bounces his ball off the wall and talks to someone Carl cannot see or hear. They are trying to claw it back, but she has already transferred it to a credit chit and sent it off. Monetary transactions are not covered by the communications blackout. It required the family ring, his eyeball and a password, and she seems to have used Colloid, the only bank the orcs use. No, sir. It is not on the chit anymore. Either way, it is too late.
